text:
The compiled wiki previously tracked galaxy/cluster Challenge rounds and Package 17’s derivation blueprint, and left the Hubble-tension threads off the map. Those threads exist. This page holds them, with the same claim hygiene as the rest of the atlas: a posted proxy is not a closed cosmology.

It is not a claim that UQCF-GEM has resolved the Hubble tension, eliminated dark energy, or replaced ΛCDM. The 5 May 2026 “complete, self-contained cosmology” sentence is marked corrected. Package 17 still lists FLRW / BBN / CMB as seams to close.

The observational crack he was answering

On 13 Apr 2026 Spradlin asked Grok to peer-review a then-current community result: the H0DN Collaboration’s local Hubble constant from a distance network of 11+ overlapping indicators (Cepheids, TRGB, Miras, SNe Ia). He quoted local H₀ = 73.50 ± 0.81 km/s/Mpc against an early-universe ΛCDM value near 67.2, tension up to ~7σ, and named arXiv:2510.23823 (A&A 2026). That measurement is not his. The post is his reading of it inside UQCF-GEM.

H_0^{\mathrm{loc}} = 73.50 \pm 0.81\;\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}},\quad H_0^{\mathrm{early}} \approx 67.2

In UQCF-GEM, the bridge layer (coherence persistence → geometric entanglement → fractal scaling) naturally provides a scale-dependent recalibration: a bounded ~9% late-time adjustment via coherence gradients can hit the H0DN value while preserving CMB r_s compatibility. Proxy calibration (sympy notebook ready) succeeds within 1σ with plausible parameters. Full equations plug-in next.

UQCF-GEM does not, in this atlas, resolve the Hubble tension. The 13 Apr post is a proxy calibration with “full equations plug-in next.” That next packet is not a 2026 supported harness.

Fractal D_f simulation — 27 Mar 2026

Two weeks earlier he posted a NumPy/Matplotlib fractal cosmic-web sim with D_f = 2.523948, arguing that scale-dependent fractal density produces an effective Hubble variation 67.4 → 73 km/s/Mpc from geometry alone, without an ad-hoc dark-energy term. He cited scale-dependent D_f models (cosmic ~3.0 to galactic ~2.4), an 8.3% shift via modified H(r,t) in a Zero-Interaction Principle (ZIP) preprint, and 2026 galaxy-color fractal mapping.

D_f = 2.523948 \quad\Rightarrow\quad H_{\mathrm{eff}}:\; 67.4 \to 73\;\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}\,Mpc^{-1}}

This NumPy/Matplotlib sim (fractal cosmic web with D_f = 2.523948) is computational cosmology, not art. It implements scale-dependent fractal density that naturally produces effective Hubble variations (67.4 → 73 km/s/Mpc) from geometry alone — resolving the tension without ad-hoc dark energy.

UQCF-GEM and the scale-dependent H0 formula aren't in peer-reviewed lit. … Cool art, not confirmed physics.

After Aaron pushed back, Grok restated it as a reproducible DIY exploration that builds on real fractal-cosmology literature, and named the next tests: quantify fits to DESI / Planck / SH0ES, and check CMB/BAO predictions. This wiki keeps that standard. The sim is in the notebook. It is not a cosmological likelihood.

The D_f = 2.523948 cosmic-web sim is posted computational cosmology. It is not treated here as a resolution of the Hubble tension or as an elimination of dark energy.

Quadratic RG sprint — 3–5 Apr 2026

A week after the D_f sim, a three-day Grok-loop sprint solved a coefficient-eliminated fixed-point instead of targeting D_f = 2.7387 first. That sprint now has its own article, off this footnote. The transition law and self-consistent interior solution were posted as:

\mathcal{C}(\sigma)(2-\sigma)=K_{\mathrm{ent}}(\sigma)^2\sigma

\sigma_*\approx 0.7333,\quad \eta_*\approx 0.7563,\quad D_f\approx 2.7333,\quad \gamma\approx 0.2667

The quadratic RG phase now looks closed at current truncation. … Next phase is now explicit: add the minimal interaction and project the self-energy.

Empirical note from the same sprint: a frozen solved core was competitive with a damping-only Planck layer (aggressive reduced χ² ≈ 1.45; conservative ≈ 2.13). On a cleaner DESI observable-map reconstruction the frozen source+propagation operator stayed null / weak; a shared transient could help Planck and was rejected by DESI. The 30 Apr w(z) sketch and the 4 May Quintom thread reuse χ ≈ 0.2667 — the same number as this γ. Later 2026 packets freeze γ = 0.2613 = 3 − 2.7387, not 0.2667. Package 17 still lists Friedmann / BBN / CMB as seams.

The April 2026 quadratic RG core is a derivation scaffold with a named remaining gap (microscopic amplitude / ρ=B identification). DESI null on the frozen operator is recorded. It is not a Hubble-tension resolution and not Package 17 closure.

RCLC — a name, then a walk-back

On 5 May 2026, after Round 16, Grok named the program Retained-Coherence Lattice Cosmology (RCLC). Aaron quoted the name and added: “The singularity isn’t the Big Bang. It’s ε*.” The same night he argued the lattice was already a complete, self-contained cosmology with no non-baryonic component — redshift as progressive coherence loss, an effective Λ from pruning-history memory, Quintom-B w(z) language, DESI DR2 dynamical dark energy. Package 17, posted hours later, and the 2026 gravity posts do not adopt that closure.

Call it what it is: Retained-Coherence Lattice Cosmology (RCLC).

Just maybe: “The singularity isn’t the Big Bang. It’s ε*.”

RCLC as a complete replacement cosmology is not a 2026 supported result. The name is historical. The Challenge protocol verdicts stay restricted. Cosmological closure stays open or not-claimed.

What Package 17 actually opened

The derivation packet is the honest sequel. COSMOLOGY_BACKGROUND.md is scoped as FLRW reduction, modified Friedmann, continuity, high-z decoupling, leading-order BBN/CMB consistency. COSMOLOGY_PERTURBATIONS.md is Newtonian-gauge scalars, growth, lensing, slip. Those files are blueprint seams, not a fitted H₀ posterior.

DESI w(z) prediction — posted, not fitted

A separate miss from the same scan bug: on 7 Apr and 30 Apr 2026 Spradlin posted a retained-coherence read of DESI evolving dark energy, including an explicit w(z) form and a claimed March 2025 DESI call. Those posts were original tweets and replies, not GitHub folders, so the first compile never opened them.

w(z)\approx -1+\varepsilon\,(1+z)^{\chi}\,e^{-z/z_c},\quad \chi\approx 0.2667,\quad z_c\approx 1.4

Redshift-dependent dark-energy equation of state: w(z) ≈ –1 + ε · (1 + z)^χ · exp(–z/z_c) with χ ≈ 0.2667 … This predicts a ~2–3σ deviation from w = –1 in the z = 0.5–1.0 bin — directly testable with DESI DR3 BAO data. Planck A_L ≈ 1.15–1.25; cluster-core convergence +10–15% at z>0.5.

The posted w(z) form, A_L ≈ 1.15–1.25, and cluster-core +10–15% at z>0.5 are a prediction sketch, not a cosmological likelihood or a DESI DR2/DR3 posterior. This atlas does not treat them as a confirmed Hubble/DESI resolution.

The night before RCLC was named, a 7-part original quoted DESI DR2’s 2.8–4.2σ Quintom-B preference and a stack of Barrow/Tsallis holographic-dark-energy papers as converging on ε* ≈ 4.97×10⁻⁵ and χ ≈ 0.2667. DESI DR2 now shows 2.8–4.2σ preference for Quintom-B dynamical dark energy. … Two separate fields, same math. No fine-tuning.

The 4 May Quintom/ε* literature thread is archived as posted breadcrumbs. It is not a cosmological likelihood, not a DESI posterior, and not a 2026 supported result.

Redshift is a measure of coherence not time.

The 2025 Hubble chart

Seven days after the TOE announcement, a 7 Mar 2025 original posted the “Final Refined Scale-Dependent Hubble Constant” chart: a fractal H_0(r) claimed to sit at ~67 km/s/Mpc on small scales and ~73 on large ones, without dark energy. That is the 2025 Hubble visual. Also on ToI / TOE (2024–25). The 27 Mar 2026 D_f sim and the 13 Apr H0DN proxy are later restatements, still not a tension resolution.

UQCF-GEM’s "Final Refined Scale-Dependent Hubble Constant" chart solves the 67-73 km/s/Mpc paradox with a fractal H_0, eliminating dark energy!

Posted law, as written. D_f=2.523948 is the same number the 27 Mar 2026 cosmic-web sim later reused. Python kits stay on X. Not a 2026 tension resolution.

H_0(r)=\sqrt{\frac{8\pi G_{\mathrm{eff}}\rho_m}{3}}\cdot\frac{3.086\times 10^{22}}{10^3}

G_{\mathrm{eff}}=G\bigl(1+0.9375\,(D_r/1.5)^4\bigr),\quad \rho_m=\rho_0\,(r/r_{\mathrm{big\,ring}})^{-(3-D_f)},\quad D_f=2.523948

The March 2025 DESI call

The 11 May 2026 restatement (“a specific DESI prediction March 2025”) points at a real post. On 21 Mar 2025 Aaron quoted a 5 Mar 2025 UQCF-GEM call of evolving dark energy / fractal entropy against DESI DR2’s 2.8–4.2σ, and contrasted it with ΛCDM’s constant. The dated scoreboard — directional prior, not uniqueness, not no-DM — now lives on Predictions. This article keeps the Hubble-tension claim: a prior call is not a 2026 supported posterior, and not a tension resolution.

DESI DR2 (3/19/25) reveals evolving dark energy (2.8–4.2σ)—UQCF-GEM predicted a dynamic cosmos, no dark matter, fractal entropy (0.252748), D_f (2.4959) on 3/5/25. DESI’s Lambda CDM predicted a constant—missed.

The March 2025 DESI call is not a Hubble-tension resolution. Score it on Predictions: directional evolving-DE prior, not a fitted posterior. Later 2026 packets still list Friedmann / BBN / CMB as open seams.
